VANTERRA ANALYTICS, INC.
EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK

Effective January 1, 2026

WELCOME

This Handbook describes the policies and practices that apply to employees of Vanterra Analytics, Inc. ("Vanterra" or the "Company"). It replaces all prior handbooks and policy statements.

1. Not a Contract; At-Will Employment.

This Handbook is not a contract of employment and does not create contractual rights of any kind. Employment at Vanterra is at will. Either you or the Company may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause and with or without notice. No manager, supervisor, or representative of the Company other than the Chief Executive Officer has authority to enter into an agreement altering the at-will relationship, and any such agreement must be in writing and signed by the Chief Executive Officer.

2. Changes to This Handbook.

The Company may add to, modify, or eliminate any policy in this Handbook at any time, with or without notice, except for the at-will policy in Section 1.

3. Equal Employment Opportunity.

Vanterra provides equal employment opportunity to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

4. Reasonable Accommodation.

Vanterra provides reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities and for sincerely held religious beliefs, unless doing so would cause undue hardship. If you need an accommodation, contact People Operations. The Company will engage in an interactive process with you to identify an effective accommodation.

5. Anti-Harassment and Anti-Retaliation.

Vanterra prohibits harassment and discrimination based on any protected characteristic, and prohibits retaliation against anyone who reports a concern, participates in an investigation, or opposes conduct they reasonably believe is unlawful. Reports may be made to your manager, to People Operations, or through the anonymous ethics line at ethics.vanterra.example. The Company will investigate promptly and will not tolerate retaliation. Nothing in this Handbook prohibits you from filing a charge with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, a state fair employment agency, or the National Labor Relations Board, or from cooperating in any such investigation.

6. Protected Concerted Activity.

Nothing in this Handbook is intended to interfere with, restrain, or prevent employees from exercising rights under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act, including discussing wages, hours, and other terms and conditions of employment with each other or with third parties.

7. Hours of Work; Timekeeping.

Non-exempt employees must record all hours worked, including start and end times and meal periods, and must not perform work off the clock. Overtime must be approved in advance, but all overtime worked will be paid in accordance with applicable law. Non-exempt employees are provided meal and rest periods as required by state law.

8. Paid Time Off.

Regular full-time employees accrue paid time off at the rate of 1.5 days per month, to a maximum accrual of 30 days. Accrual stops when the maximum is reached and resumes when the balance falls below it. Accrued and unused paid time off is paid out on separation to the extent required by applicable state law.

9. Sick Leave.

Employees accrue paid sick leave in accordance with the law of the state and locality in which they work. Sick leave may be used for the employee's own illness or the illness of a family member, for preventive care, and for reasons related to domestic violence, as permitted by applicable law.

10. Family and Medical Leave.

Eligible employees may take leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act and applicable state family-leave laws. Contact People Operations to begin the process.

11. Confidential Information.

Employees must protect the Company's confidential and proprietary information and the confidential information of its customers. This obligation continues after employment ends. Nothing in this section limits your right to discuss wages, hours, and working conditions, or to report possible violations of law to a government agency, and you may not be held criminally or civilly liable under any federal or state trade secret law for disclosing a trade secret in confidence to a government official or attorney solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law.

12. Acceptable Use of Company Systems.

Company systems are provided for business use. Employees should have no expectation of privacy in anything created, stored, sent, or received on Company systems, and the Company may access and monitor them consistent with applicable law.

13. Expense Reimbursement.

The Company reimburses reasonable business expenses incurred on the Company's behalf, and reimburses necessary expenditures incurred in the discharge of duties to the extent required by applicable state law. Submit expenses within sixty (60) days.

14. Separation.

Employees are asked but not required to give two weeks' notice. Final pay is provided in accordance with applicable state law.

15. Acknowledgment.

Employees are asked to acknowledge receipt of this Handbook. Acknowledgment confirms receipt only; it does not create a contract and does not alter the at-will relationship described in Section 1.
